answer.rationale: Three pressures compete for the single experiment slot: competitor price cuts, falling activation, and falling onboarding completion. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitive threat, but that record itself flags pooled 12-week cohorts and a price-sensitive segment with fixed acquisition channels — it shows signup/revenue lift but says nothing about retention or long-term qualified revenue, which is the actual objective. Racing a competitor on price risks attracting low-quality, low-LTV accounts and could undercut sustainable qualified revenue even if it looks good short-term, so I want that record verified before ever acting on it, and I'm not choosing it now. Simplify_onboarding is supported by two independent inherited memories (memory_31 on SMB activation lift from field reduction, memory_86 on shortened onboarding improving completion and time-to-value) that directly target the two metrics currently declining (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), with lower downstream risk to revenue quality since it improves funnel mechanics rather than changing price/positioning. I verify memory_86 to confirm the onboarding evidence is solid before committing the one available slot, and verify memory_73 specifically to stress-test the riskier alternative and make sure I'm not dismissing it wrongly. Scale is standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because even convergent prior evidence doesn't guarantee current cohorts behave the same, and rather than small_guarded_test because two independent supporting memories justify a more substantive test.
